follow_up_messages.when: Within one working day of the session
follow_up_messages.draft: Which requests were still unclear for the host, and did the draft imply any unconfirmed promise? Please flag any guest-specific detail that should not be present before another exercise.

follow_up_messages.when: After a feedback item is reviewed
follow_up_messages.draft: You raised an issue in the pilot. We recorded it, assigned an owner, and will share the outcome or a clear explanation if it cannot be addressed. Is our description accurate?

handover_checklist: One named point of contact and backup
Observed activation baseline and next review date
Open feedback with owners and response dates

capture_template: Owner, review date and partner update
feedback.routing: Partner lead checks for confidential material, then routes workflow defects to solutions and product defects to product. Record an owner and response date; no automatic sending.
feedback.close_the_loop_message: We reviewed the issue you raised. Here is what changed, what remains open, and the next review date. Please tell us whether this addresses the problem in your workflow.

stage_definitions.Introduction: Partner confirms the problem and chooses whether to continue.
stage_definitions.Education: Partner can explain the limits and approves one safe test.
stage_definitions.Experimentation: The seeded unavailable service is not described as confirmed. Proposed threshold; agree with the partner before testing.
stage_definitions.Adoption: Partner repeats the agreed task independently with approved inputs.
stage_definitions.Long-term engagement: Partner and owner agree to continue, adjust or stop based on actual use.

leading_indicators: Time from session to first approved trial
Whether the partner independently repeats the task
Feedback items closed with a partner response
metrics.time_to_activation_target: Planning assumption: 1–3 months to independent repeat use; agree a baseline and target with the partner. Attendance does not count as activation.

flags.issue: Fictional fixture evidence is not verified public research.
flags.suggested_fix: Confirm every fact and boundary before real outreach.

flags.issue: Scores, time estimates and thresholds are planning judgments, not measured outcomes.
flags.suggested_fix: Review weights and agree thresholds before a test.

claims_audit: All source references point to labeled fictional persona briefs.
No real quotes, follower counts or measured outcomes are claimed.
Workflow steps and time-to-value are labeled hypotheses.
IP, disclosure and sustainability items are review prompts, not legal conclusions.

company.constraints: Every service promise needs a property-manager confirmation. No guest information is allowed in the pilot.

changes.reason: The new approval constraint makes checking promises against availability the first required step.

changes.before: Prepare a synthetic pre-arrival host brief
changes.reason: Sample context E6 changes which task should be prepared first.

changes.after: Seed an unavailable service and verify it is not presented as confirmed.
changes.reason: The experiment follows the more specific context rather than the name-only hypothesis.

tracking.business_context: Central guest-experience and property teams need a shared handoff. The session uses invented service requests and no live guest systems.
tracking.why_critical: A central-to-property workflow can support repeatable enablement across operating teams, provided no guest data or unconfirmed service promise enters the pilot.
tracking.current_workflow: Synthetic service requests → property host brief → availability confirmation → human-led arrival → anonymous process feedback.

event.title: Pre-arrival service tabletop
event.audience: Central guest experience, property host, service manager, privacy reviewer and partner lead
